papers.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
papers.abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. The directions of this tradeoff are partly implied by the rule; its magnitude depends on reviewer transitions and upstream proposal states. A prospective validation then gives the reviewer an explicit choice to retain, replace, or escalate. This eliminates correct-proposal corruption for Qwen, but Mistral still replaces all 48 correct proposals; Qwen also declines every welfare-only repair that Mistral frequently attempts. Thus interface design changes reviewer behavior but is not a model-independent safeguard. The result is not that restricted review is universally better. It is that reviewer competence, action interface, and binding jurisdiction jointly determine both the correction domain and the corruption surface.

translation.title: 谁可以推翻智能体？LLM 审查机构中的证据门控权威
translation.abstract: 多智能体语言模型系统常通过添加审查者来改进上游智能体的决策，但审查者既可能修复错误，也可能替换原本正确的决策。我们将此视为一个机构管辖权问题：在相同的提案、任务信息、模型和审查输出条件下，何时应授权审查者使其建议具有约束力？我们比较了宽泛的推翻权限与一种证据门控机制——后者仅在审查者产出机械上有效的记录（证明存在约束违反及合规修复）后才允许替换。在两个本地运行的开源权重模型、96 个空间政策任务和一个 96 任务组合迁移基准上，该门控大幅减少了对正确提案的破坏，同时保留了大部分对违规的修复。这一权衡的方向部分由规则决定，其幅度则取决于审查者的状态转移和上游提案状态。前瞻性验证进一步赋予审查者保留、替换或升级的显式选择：这消除了 Qwen 的正确提案破坏，但 Mistral 仍替换了全部 48 个正确提案；Qwen 还拒绝了 Mistral 频繁尝试的纯福利修复。因此，接口设计会改变审查者行为，但并非与模型无关的保障。结论并非受限审查普遍更优，而是审查者能力、行动接口和约束性管辖权共同决定了纠正域与破坏面。
translation.brief: 研究多智能体系统中审查者何时有权推翻上游智能体决策，提出仅在审查者提供有效违规证据时才允许替换的证据门控机制。

papers.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
papers.abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority. We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model. In a 216-decision ablation across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.7 Flash, verified tool-health state reduced mean observable policy regret by 96.9% against a same-shape neutral control (4,252 ms to 131 ms) and raised single-dispatch completion from 69.4% to 95.8%. In a separate 27-decision end-to-end replication with live local TCP/HTTP execution, OpenTelemetry client spans, and Toxiproxy-injected faults, verified state reduced mean regret from 8,956 ms to 0 ms (zero excess observable operational cost) and completed the live action in 9/9 model-by-fault cases versus 5/9 for the neutral control. These studies establish the tools-and-network instance of Agent Harness Awareness: selected host telemetry materially improves pre-dispatch operational choice. Runtime state, hardware pressure, economics, retry-aware recovery, and heterogeneous selection remain open empirical extensions of the same architecture.

translation.title: 智能体线束感知：将经验证的遥测数据转化为工具使用智能体的运行控制
translation.abstract: 工具描述告诉智能体某个动作能做什么，但未必揭示该动作在使用时刻是否健康或适用。执行线束（harness）通过监控器、追踪和近期故障往往掌握这些信息，而选择下一步动作的模型却不知道。我们称这一差距为运行盲区。我们提出 Agent Harness Awareness，一种信任分离的设计：宿主在关键动作前提供小而新鲜、经验证的状态快照，同时保留测量、执行、评估和最终分发权限。我们用 ToolRoute 测试其工具与网络实例——一个受控隔离基准，保持任务和候选语义不变，仅改变模型可获得的运行信息。在跨 GPT-5.6 Sol、Claude Sonnet 5 和 Gemini 3.7 Flash 的 216 决策消融中，经验证的工具健康状态使平均可观测策略遗憾相对同形状中性对照降低 96.9%（4,252 ms 降至 131 ms），单次分发完成率从 69.4% 提升至 95.8%。在另一项 27 决策的端到端复现实验（含本地 TCP/HTTP 实时执行、OpenTelemetry 客户端 span 和 Toxiproxy 注入故障）中，经验证状态将平均遗憾从 8,956 ms 降至 0 ms，并在 9/9 的模型-故障组合中完成实时动作，而中性对照仅为 5/9。这些研究确立了 Agent Harness Awareness 的工具与网络实例：精选的宿主遥测能显著改善分发前的运行选择。运行时状态、硬件压力、经济性、重试感知恢复和异构选择仍是该架构的开放实证扩展。
translation.brief: 针对模型无法感知工具运行健康状况的运行盲区问题，提出由宿主在关键动作前提供经验证状态快照的信任分离设计。

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
papers.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. Existing schedulers require a fully known pipeline graph, while edge resource-management methods rely on parametric or stationary demand models, and neither fits the unknown, non-stationary profiles of agentic pipelines. We formalize this setting as the uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration problem, where the goal is to reserve, at dispatch time, compute and bandwidth allocations that cover actual pipeline demands, and to verify that the pipeline can meet its deadline, each with a prescribed probability. We then propose Conformal Reservation for Orchestration (CRO), an online algorithm that translates a sliding window of past execution traces into dispatch-time resource allocations with finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees via conformal prediction. Simulations over heterogeneous task mixes with multi-modal and heavy-tailed profiles show that CRO is the only evaluated method that simultaneously satisfies target probabilistic coverage across all risk levels while, among coverage-feasible methods, attaining the lowest over-reservation, roughly halving the resource waste of the Chebyshev-bound baseline.

translation.title: 面向 Agentic AI 系统的不确定性感知资源编排
translation.abstract: 由大语言模型（LLM）驱动的 Agentic AI 系统以自主多步流水线方式执行，动态调用工具、将观测整合进记忆并迭代，直到任务完成或资源预算耗尽。与图结构固定的经典工作流不同，此类流水线的总计算、带宽和端到端延迟需求在分发时未知：它们在运行时由中间观测和随机 token 采样涌现，形成重尾、多峰的随机变量。这种不可预测性使基础设施编排者陷入两难：供给不足可能导致执行中途限流和违反截止期限，供给过度则浪费稀缺的边缘或云端容量。现有调度器要求完全已知的流水线图，而边缘资源管理方法依赖参数化或平稳的需求模型，均不适用于 agentic 流水线未知、非平稳的需求特征。我们将该场景形式化为不确定性感知 agentic 编排问题：目标是在分发时预留能覆盖实际流水线需求的计算与带宽分配，并以规定概率验证流水线能满足截止期限。我们随后提出 Conformal Reservation for Orchestration（CRO），一种在线算法，通过 conformal prediction 将过去执行轨迹的滑动窗口转化为具有有限样本、分布无关覆盖保证的分发时资源分配。在具有多峰和重尾特征的异构任务混合仿真中，CRO 是唯一在所有风险水平上同时满足目标概率覆盖的方法，且在覆盖可行的方法中实现最低的过度预留，资源浪费约为 Chebyshev 界基线的一半。
translation.brief: 针对 agentic 流水线资源需求在分发时未知且非平稳的问题，提出基于 conformal prediction 的在线算法 CRO，提供分布无关覆盖保证的资源预留。

papers.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. Ablations indicate benefits from both retrieval timing and gap-specific query signals, and a live web-search experiment shows that the timing advantage persists across retrieval backends. For specialist recruitment, self-triggered adaptation is unreliable, whereas Challenger-triggered recruitment raises GPT-4.1-mini MedQA accuracy from 46% to 54%, with positive direction on all tested generalization datasets. Naively combining retrieval and specialist recruitment degrades performance, highlighting the need to coordinate adaptive intervention channels. These results show that when and why external resources are recruited is a key design choice in multi-agent medical reasoning.

translation.title: 面向医疗多智能体推理的挑战感知知识招募与元智能体监督
translation.abstract: 大语言模型在标准医疗问答上表现强劲，但在更难的推理任务上性能下降，此时多智能体辩论往往不敌强大的单模型提示。我们认为一个关键局限在于：现有系统仅根据问题本身选择专家和检索知识，而非根据推理过程中涌现的缺口。我们提出挑战感知的自适应招募：一个外部 CHALLENGER 检查不断演化的推理轨迹，识别具体的事实或专业知识缺口，这些信号触发针对性的知识检索或讨论中途的专家招募。在 MEDAGENTSBENCH 困难子集（涵盖九个生物医学数据集的 862 个问题）上，预先检索收益甚微，而挑战感知的中途检索表现更好；在多专家骨干上，它在 9 个数据集中的 8 个上提升准确率，并比仅 Challenger 方案高出 6 个百分点。消融实验表明检索时机和针对缺口的查询信号均有贡献，实时网络搜索实验显示时机优势在不同检索后端上均成立。对于专家招募，自我触发的自适应不可靠，而 Challenger 触发的招募将 GPT-4.1-mini 的 MedQA 准确率从 46% 提升至 54%，且在所有测试的泛化数据集上方向为正。简单组合检索与专家招募会降低性能，凸显了协调自适应干预通道的必要性。这些结果表明，何时以及为何招募外部资源是多智能体医疗推理中的关键设计选择。
translation.brief: 针对多智能体医疗推理仅凭问题选择专家和知识的局限，提出由外部 CHALLENGER 识别推理缺口并触发中途检索与专家招募的机制。

papers.title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving. Most such systems orchestrate frozen model checkpoints, and most decide what to resolve locally and what to escalate using a confidence signal produced by a forward-deployed model. We give a closed-form condition for when no threshold on that signal makes a tiered cascade worthwhile relative to sending every query to the backstop. Modeling the routing decision as a binary test and separating local from escalation cost through an architecture cost ratio $\kappa$, we derive a feasibility condition bracketed by a signal-free floor, below which a cascade is feasible at any signal quality, and a perfect-signal ceiling, above which none is. Read along the $\kappa$ axis the condition inverts: where local compute is billed, cost binds, matching a recent empirical finding; where it is sunk, on decentralized hardware, feasibility becomes unconditional and signal quality instead sets what the cascade achieves. We turn the condition into three design requirements that existing trained-in primitives satisfy only in isolation, and we propose, as future work, a co-designed architecture and a protocol to test it. The condition and the inversion hold independently of that architecture; they are the paper's contribution.

translation.title: 置信度门控分层 LLM 推理的可行性条件
translation.abstract: 分层推理将大语言模型计算分布在从端侧、边缘硬件到数据中心的设备层级上，日益被视为实现更廉价、更低延迟、更隐私的服务路径。大多数此类系统编排冻结的模型检查点，并使用由前置部署模型产生的置信度信号来决定本地解决还是升级。我们给出了一个闭式条件，刻画何时对该信号设置任何阈值都无法使分层级联相对将所有查询发送到兜底层更有价值。将路由决策建模为二元检验，并通过架构成本比 $\kappa$ 分离本地与升级成本，我们推导出一个由无信号下界和完美信号上界夹住的可行性条件：低于下界时级联在任何信号质量下均可行，高于上界时则不可行。沿 $\kappa$ 轴读取该条件会发生反转：当本地计算被计费时，成本成为约束，这与近期一项实证发现相符；当本地计算为沉没成本（如去中心化硬件）时，可行性变为无条件，而信号质量则决定级联所能达到的效果。我们将该条件转化为三个设计要求——现有训练内原语只能各自满足其一——并提出作为未来工作的协同设计架构及测试协议。该条件及其反转独立于该架构成立，它们是本文的贡献。
translation.brief: 针对置信度门控分层 LLM 推理何时优于全部上送兜底层的问题，推导出以架构成本比刻画的闭式可行性条件及其反转性质。

papers.title: LLM-based NPCs in Video Games: A Systematic Mapping Study
papers.abstract: For decades, non-player characters (NPCs) have been driven by rule-based systems whose personalities and interactions are scripted before release. Large language models (LLMs) promise NPCs that converse openly, adapt to new situations, and behave in ways developers did not fully author, prompting a wave of research and commercial experimentation. Yet the field lacks a unified picture of what has been built, how well it works, and at what cost. We address this gap with a systematic mapping study of 377 papers from the academic literature, yielding 42 papers analysed against a main research question and ten sub-questions across four thematic axes. We provide the first quantitative characterisation of component adoption, latency, safety coverage, and reproducibility: short-term memory and world-state grounding are near-universal (60% and 69%), whereas long-term memory (31%), reflection (38%), and retrieval-augmented generation (14%) remain rare, and response times span 2.6 to 15 seconds. Finally, we identify six structural barriers to commercial adoption and offer evidence-based recommendations for developers and researchers.

papers.title: LIBRA: Programmatic Induction of Executable Tool Libraries
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly retrieve tools from large catalogs, yet most retrievers rank each tool independently by request similarity. For multi tool tasks, this recovers the goal matching tool while omitting prerequisite tools required by the this http URL introduce LIBRA, a framework for Library Induction by Runtime Assembly that turns a flat tool catalog into an executable tool library. An LLM proposes per tool contracts of candidate invocations, reusable outputs and state changes, and success conditions; LIBRA then tests these compositions in a sandbox and retains the relations supported at runtime. Constructed before user queries, the library requires no dependency annotations, tool use trajectories, or task specific training, and supports both one-shot and agentic retrieval. On AppWorld, BFCL, and SciToolEval, LIBRA improves one-shot Recall and NDCG over the same dense retriever by 7.9 and 3.7 percentage points on average. Within ToolReAGt, it yields corresponding gains of 4.5 and 2.9 points after ten retrieval iterations.

papers.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
papers.abstract: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. We present Jev-AD, which pairs Jev, a typed decision model that answers predefined questions with probabilities, not generated text, with a language world model that predicts for every candidate action how nearby vehicles move over the next two seconds. Code turns these predictions into foreseen consequences, which Jev compares instead of inferring them from coordinates. In simulated highway merging (500 car-episodes), this foresight lowers the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision, and Jev-AD achieves the passenger's intent in 93% of free-form command trials. In 500 replayed real-world NGSIM episodes, foresight lowers the collision rate from 48.2% to 2.8%, and the world model, learned from this traffic, foresees 93% of dangerous actions. Project page: this https URL.

papers.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
papers.abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience lifecycle across 18 interactive environments. It distinguishes structural experience about how an environment is organized and accessed from rule experience about reusable principles and constraints that guide decisions across tasks. To study how experience is acquired, reused, and revised, we propose an experience-first construction approach. It builds task streams around shared experience and introduces silent environmental changes. We evaluate task performance and track changes in saved experience throughout each stream. Across 20 models, we find that retained experience improves task performance, but agents struggle to keep it current as environments change. Even when the required experience is correctly recorded, agents do not always complete tasks successfully. These findings identify selective maintenance and effective use as complementary challenges for long-lived agents.

papers.title: Agentic Behavior Engineering: A Design-by-Contract Methodology for Specifying, Verifying, and Governing Enterprise AI Agents
papers.abstract: Enterprise teams that deploy large language model (LLM) agents inherit a maintenance problem that traditional testing does not address. The model is non-deterministic, but the larger risk is that most of what changes an agent's behavior (a retired model version, a revised policy, an upstream schema change, a prompt edit meant to fix one case) originates outside the owning team and is discovered as a production defect rather than caught as a regression. This paper presents Agentic Behavior Engineering (ABE), a platform-agnostic methodology that treats observable agent behavior, rather than the prompt or the model, as the version-controlled engineering artifact. ABE adapts Design by Contract to non-deterministic systems. A specification-only behavior contract with stable rule identifiers states what the agent must do, must not do, and when it must abstain for lack of evidence; a lightweight scenario library turns each rule into concrete situations; and every engineering artifact (tests, runtime policies, telemetry) references the contract in one direction only, so that specification and implementation can change independently without drifting apart. The method organizes the work into five responsibilities (Specify, Ground, Control, Verify, Observe), treats missing evidence and a verified negative as different things, enforces authority outside the model, gates releases on per-scenario pass^k reliability rather than aggregate accuracy, and classifies every production run against the contract so that each finding routes to the asset that must change. We illustrate the method with an executable capacity-allocation boundary suite and a constructed worked example of a product-review approval workflow.

The model is non-deterministic, but the larger risk is that most of what changes an agent's behavior (a retired model version, a revised policy, an upstream schema change, a prompt edit meant to fix one case) originates outside the owning team and is discovered as a production defect rather than caught as a regression. This paper presents Agentic Behavior Engineering (ABE), a platform-agnostic methodology that treats observable agent behavior, rather than the prompt or the model, as the version-controlled engineering artifact. ABE adapts Design by Contract to non-deterministic systems. A specification-only behavior contract with stable rule identifiers states what the agent must do, must not do, and when it must abstain for lack of evidence; a lightweight scenario library turns each rule into concrete situations; and every engineering artifact (tests, runtime policies, telemetry) references the contract in one direction only, so that specification and implementation can change independently without drifting apart. The method organizes the work into five responsibilities (Specify, Ground, Control, Verify, Observe), treats missing evidence and a verified negative as different things, enforces authority outside the model, gates releases on per-scenario pass^k reliability rather than aggregate accuracy, and classifies every production run against the contract so that each finding routes to the asset that must change. We illustrate the method with an executable capacity-allocation boundary suite and a constructed worked example of a product-review approval workflow.

papers.title: Hybrid LLM-Deterministic Pipelines for Enterprise-Scale Code Migration at Bloomberg
papers.abstract: Large organizations carry a long tail of infrastructure migrations that are worth doing but rarely urgent enough to compete with feature work, because each one costs significant engineering time per repository. This paper reports on our industrial experience from Automated Uplift, a multi-month initiative applying LLM-assisted migration pipelines across thousands of Bloomberg repositories. We examine two distinct production campaigns: a heterogeneous Python packaging migration (approx. 1,900 candidate repositories) and a uniform C++ build system migration (approx. 6,700 candidate repositories). Together, these campaigns generated 2,333 pull requests, resulting in 729 successful migrations. We detail our hybrid architectural solution which maximizes deterministic processing, confines the LLM to bounded file transformations within a pre-computed context, and incorporates runtime production telemetry (such as execution logs and usage traces). Our findings show that generating migrations turned out to be the easier part; the bottleneck was the cost, for owning teams, of reviewing, testing, and deploying them. These costs were lowered when changes could be verified directly in the pipeline before opening a PR (as with C++ compilation and test validation), and when the population was uniform enough for fixes to carry over from one repository to the next. We conclude by distilling our experience and findings into actionable, transferable patterns for architecting hybrid LLM-deterministic pipelines and scaling code migrations across the enterprise

translation.title: Bloomberg 企业级代码迁移中的 LLM 与确定性混合流水线
translation.abstract: 大型组织都背负着一系列值得做但紧迫性不足的基础设施迁移长尾任务，因为每项迁移在每个代码仓库上都要耗费大量工程时间。本文报告了我们从 Automated Uplift 项目中获得的企业实践经验，这是一项历时数月、在数千个 Bloomberg 代码仓库中应用 LLM 辅助迁移流水线的计划。我们考察了两个不同的生产环境迁移活动：一个异构的 Python 打包迁移（约 1,900 个候选仓库）和一个统一的 C++ 构建系统迁移（约 6,700 个候选仓库）。两项活动共产生了 2,333 个 pull request，成功完成 729 次迁移。我们详细介绍了混合架构方案：最大化确定性处理，将 LLM 限制在预计算上下文内的有界文件转换中，并引入运行时生产遥测数据（如执行日志和使用轨迹）。我们的发现表明，生成迁移其实是较容易的部分；真正的瓶颈是各负责团队在审查、测试和部署这些迁移时的成本。当变更可以在打开 PR 之前直接在流水线中验证（如 C++ 编译和测试验证），且仓库群体足够同质、修复方案可以从一个仓库复用到下一个仓库时，这些成本得以降低。最后，我们将经验与发现提炼为可操作、可迁移的模式，用于构建混合 LLM-确定性流水线并在企业范围内扩展代码迁移。
translation.brief: 解决企业大规模代码迁移中人工成本高的问题，采用最大化确定性处理、将 LLM 限制在有界转换并结合生产遥测的混合流水线架构。

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. We assess six AI tools across four stages: finding relevant articles, interpreting them, synthesizing across them, and proposing future research. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus. In the initial searches, five tools collectively identified 57 articles, with the best individual tool finding 42. Institutional library access increased discovery from 42 to 82 articles for Codex and from 15 to 79 for Claude Code. Given the complete corpus of 102 PDFs, three tools correctly identified all 18 articles discussing the Spanish plume substantially, but incorrectly classified 40% to 79% of the 84 passing mentions as substantial. The same three tools produced syntheses evaluated blindly by two domain experts. Although largely accurate, the syntheses provided limited insight and sometimes contained unsupported claims, quotation errors, and exaggerated statements of consensus. Finally, all three tools proposed research directions broader than the Spanish plume literature, although two approached questions identified in the benchmark review. No single tool performed best across all tasks. We provide eight recommendations for researchers using AI tools in literature reviews. Our findings suggest that LLMs can assist with discovering and interpreting scientific literature, particularly when institutional access is available, but cannot replace expert judgment in evaluating evidence or synthesizing research.

translation.title: 大语言模型能审阅科学文献吗？基于 102 篇文章基准的测试
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于辅助科学文献综述，但现有评估往往只考察单个任务，而非整个综述流程。我们在四个阶段评估了六种 AI 工具：查找相关文章、解读文章、跨文章综合以及提出未来研究方向。基准是一篇已发表的关于 Spanish plume 天气型态的综述及其 102 篇文章语料库。在初始检索中，五种工具共识别出 57 篇文章，表现最好的单个工具找到 42 篇。机构图书馆访问权限使 Codex 的发现量从 42 篇提升到 82 篇，Claude Code 从 15 篇提升到 79 篇。在给定完整的 102 篇 PDF 语料后，三种工具正确识别出全部 18 篇实质性讨论 Spanish plume 的文章，但将 84 篇仅顺带提及的文章中的 40% 至 79% 错误地归类为实质性讨论。同样的三种工具生成的综合报告由两位领域专家盲评。虽然大体准确，但这些综合报告提供的洞见有限，有时包含无依据的断言、引用错误和夸大的共识表述。最后，三种工具提出的研究方向都比 Spanish plume 文献更宽泛，尽管其中两个工具接近了基准综述中识别出的问题。没有任何单一工具在所有任务上表现最佳。我们为在文献综述中使用 AI 工具的研究者提供了八条建议。我们的发现表明，LLM 可以辅助发现和解读科学文献，尤其是在有机构访问权限的情况下，但无法替代专家在评估证据或综合研究时的判断。
translation.brief: 评估 LLM 工具能否完成完整文献综述流程，以一篇 102 篇文章的真实综述为基准，在检索、解读、综合和提出方向四个阶段进行系统测试。

papers.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage. Empirical experiments across varying numbers of objectives demonstrate the effectiveness of OGC-DPO over existing active preference learning methods under the same annotation cost. Further analysis demonstrates that informative conflicts, rather than being uniformly harmful, provide a useful policy training signal.

translation.title: 面向多目标对齐的目标条件化主动偏好学习
translation.abstract: 将大语言模型（LLM）与多个目标（如有用性、无害性和诚实性）对齐，通常需要对每个目标分别进行偏好判断，使标注成本随目标数量线性增长。主动偏好学习可以通过选择那些预期最能改变策略的比较样本 来降低这一成本。现有方法要么缺乏面向多目标设置的目标感知查询选择机制，要么将冲突的偏好视为有害而将其排除在训练数据之外。我们提出 OGC-DPO（Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO），这是一个主动学习框架，它将每个（响应对，目标）组合视为独立查询，并通过策略自身的隐式梯度来衡量其信息量，而无需依赖外部奖励模型。OGC-DPO 随后选择最能扩展各目标梯度覆盖范围的查询。在不同目标数量下的实证实验表明，在相同标注成本下，OGC-DPO 优于现有的主动偏好学习方法。进一步分析表明，有信息量的冲突并非一律有害，反而能为策略训练提供有用的信号。
translation.brief: 解决多目标对齐中偏好标注成本随目标数线性增长的问题，提出 OGC-DPO 框架，利用策略隐式梯度衡量（响应对，目标）组合的信息量并选择最能扩展梯度覆盖的查询。

papers.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
papers.abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling stale or conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources. We introduce SlackBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on realistic research and engineering workflows that require joint reasoning over workplace communication and evolving repository state. Grounded in privacy-preserving reenactments of real academic research projects, SlackBench provides reproducible environments with realistic multi-party dialogue, evolving decisions, and corresponding code changes grounded in GitHub repositories and Google Docs. It contains 140 queries spanning heterogeneous-source agentic search, abstention on unanswerable or false-premise questions, goal-directed summarization, and circumstance inference over long conversations. These tasks are not reducible to static corpus question answering: agents must determine which conversations matter, traverse threads, inspect repository state, and synthesize evidence across communication and code artifacts. Across 33 frontier models and agent harnesses, the best system scores around 80% and most agents score below 66%, highlighting substantial headroom for improvement. SlackBench thus provides an extensible framework for evaluating agents in collaborative work environments. The SlackBench dataset is available at this https URL .

translation.title: SlackBench：基于真实代码仓库的协作项目智能体基准测试
translation.abstract: AI 智能体正在成为可以浏览网页、编写代码、运行实验并在长周期内协助人类的数字同事。然而现有基准与真实知识工作存在差距：许多基准依赖合成数据或孤立任务，忽略了协作项目中复杂的多方动态——关键信息散布在对话、代码和不断演进的决策之中。即使是简单的工作场所问题，也可能需要定位相关频道和私信、从冗长讨论中恢复上下文、检查仓库状态、调和过时或冲突的证据，并跨来源进行综合。我们提出 SlackBench，一个评估智能体在真实研究与工程工作流中表现的基准，这些工作流需要对工作场所沟通和不断演进的仓库状态进行联合推理。SlackBench 基于对真实学术研究项目的隐私保护重演，提供可复现的环境，包含真实的多方对话、不断演进的决策，以及基于 GitHub 仓库和 Google Docs 的相应代码变更。它包含 140 个查询，涵盖异构来源的智能体搜索、对不可回答或错误前提问题的拒答、目标导向的摘要，以及长对话中的情境推断。这些任务无法简化为静态语料库问答：智能体必须判断哪些对话重要、遍历讨论线程、检查仓库状态，并跨沟通与代码工件综合证据。在 33 个前沿模型和智能体框架上的测试中，最佳系统得分约 80%，大多数智能体得分低于 66%，凸显出巨大的改进空间。SlackBench 因此为评估协作工作环境中的智能体提供了一个可扩展的框架。SlackBench 数据集可在该 https URL 获取。
translation.brief: 解决现有基准无法评估智能体在真实协作项目中跨沟通与代码联合推理的问题，构建基于真实学术项目隐私保护重演的 SlackBench 基准，包含 140 个多源推理查询。

papers.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
papers.abstract: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret text but lack numerical precision, while Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are quantitatively accurate but cannot reason about the effects of text. Moreover, the lack of large-scale paired multimodal datasets limits progress in bridging this gap. In this work, we address this challenge by providing a scalable approach for generating realistic multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs. Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. We align the two models in stages, first fine-tuning the LLM via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward tied to covariate-induced improvement in forecasting performance, and then fine-tuning the TSFM on covariates generated by the aligned LLM. Our experiments show that models trained on our synthetic multimodal corpus generalize to real benchmarks spanning finance, economics, weather, traffic, and security. Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o. Code, checkpoints, and the evaluation datasets are publicly available.

translation.title: TSFM 遇见 LLM：作为协变量的上下文
translation.abstract: 文本信息在现实世界的时间序列数据集中无处不在，以新闻、报告和注释的形式出现，其中蕴含着仅凭数值历史无法推导的关键预测信号。大语言模型（LLM）能够解读文本但缺乏数值精度，而时间序列基础模型（TSFM）数值精确但无法推理文本的影响。此外，大规模成对多模态数据集的缺乏也限制了弥合这一鸿沟的进展。在本工作中，我们通过一种可扩展的方法来应对这一挑战：利用 LLM 为真实世界时间序列添加标注，从而生成逼真的多模态数据集。在此基础上，我们提出 Context as Covariates（CoCo）预测框架，其中 LLM 将其文本推理提炼为数值化的预测和置信度协变量，用以引导 TSFM 骨干网络，从而同时发挥 LLM 和 TSFM 的优势。我们分阶段对齐两个模型：首先通过 Group Relative Policy Optimization（GRPO）微调 LLM，其奖励与协变量带来的预测性能提升挂钩；然后在由对齐后的 LLM 生成的协变量上微调 TSFM。实验表明，在我们的合成多模态语料上训练的模型能够泛化到涵盖金融、经济、天气、交通和安全领域的真实基准。值得注意的是，以 Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 作为 LLM、Chronos2 作为 TSFM 的 CoCo，相比 GPT-4o 等最先进的 TSFM 和 LLM 预测器，MAE 最高提升 12%。代码、检查点和评估数据集均已公开。
translation.brief: 解决时间序列预测中 LLM 缺乏数值精度而 TSFM 无法利用文本的问题，提出 CoCo 框架，让 LLM 将文本推理转化为协变量引导 TSFM，并通过 GRPO 分阶段对齐两模型。

papers.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
papers.abstract: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. We also propose BACE (Belief-Aware Critic with Epistemic tracking), a lightweight action chooser method on top of a frozen LM backbone, and show that BACE more consistently chooses the optimal number of clarifying questions than methods such as GRPO and ArCHer.

papers.title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.abstract: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Building on the single-agent construction that embeds control barrier function (CBF) constraints into reverse-diffusion updates, we: (i) formalize joint safe sets as intersections of per-agent and pairwise barrier sets; (ii) derive centralized and decentralized (communication-aware) constrained denoising procedures with provable invariance under mild assumptions; (iii) address local-trap and deadlock phenomena via time-varying specifications and liveness CBFs; and (iv) develop a lightweight benchmarking suite including a multi-agent Maze2D domain. Empirically, MA-SafeDiffuser reduces violation counts relative to unconstrained diffusion baselines, while retaining planning quality. We provide algorithms, proofs, and reference implementations.

papers.title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction
papers.abstract: LLMs can repair noisy OCR transcripts of historical documents, but they also change text that was already correct. We propose EditVeto, a veto gate placed after a full-context LLM rewrite. The rewrite is character-aligned to the OCR input, its differences are split into blocks, and a 0.6B-parameter gate keeps or reverts each block. An oracle analysis motivates the design: given the true error locations, per-span generation is worse than no correction, whereas vetoing a full rewrite's edits helps. Trained on rewrites by two Qwen3 models and evaluated, frozen, on the eight HIPE-OCRepair-2026 test sets, the gate improves all five rewriters tested, two of them unseen in training: weighted cMER falls by 0.0026-0.0044 and the preference score rises by 0.15-0.25 (paired bootstrap, p ~ 0.0002 each). On published competition outputs it lowers cMER for three of four teams but raises it for the winning run (0.0050 to 0.0065). In a second, disclosed test look, a retrained gate still improves LoRA-tuned rewriters (cMER -0.0011 to -0.0021), and an ensemble of their gated edits reaches a cMER of 0.0069 and a preference score of 0.928, mostly through fine-tuning and pooling rather than gating. Built only on public models and data, it is behind the winner (0.0050) and tied with the second-ranked run (0.0071), both from the only team using domain pre-training, and ahead of all other published runs. A third, secondary look shows the unchanged gate improving zero-shot Qwen3.8-27B (cMER 0.0114 to 0.0108) but only the preference score of its LoRA-tuned version.

papers.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
papers.abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. A 'writer' model with specific tools creates a complete data science project including downloading, cleaning, and analyzing a dataset, and writing a short paper about it. The project is executed and a 'grader' model evaluates it. The writer can then revise its submission, and this repeats for a total of three rounds. We consider seven models from five developers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and this http URL. Each model is both a writer and a grader, so there are 49 writer-grader pairs and we run each pair three times. Of the 147 initial submissions, 107 run and render, and the average score increases from 59 per cent to 76 per cent after the final round of feedback. By writer the extent of the increase ranges from 3 percentage points for Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to 46 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5, and by grader it ranges from 13 percentage points for Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash to 32 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5. When a model grades its own writing the score tends to be about 9 percentage points higher than the average of what the other models give it. About half of the difference that we see from round to round is within the grader's own noise. Feedback generally results in the highest marks, but even just having the chance to revise, or having the additional budget, in terms of time or tool calls, without any feedback, results in considerable increases for some of the models but not for others. We find that how much such a loop helps depends on which model plays which role, but weaker models generally do not improve stronger models.

We consider seven models from five developers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and this http URL. Each model is both a writer and a grader, so there are 49 writer-grader pairs and we run each pair three times. Of the 147 initial submissions, 107 run and render, and the average score increases from 59 per cent to 76 per cent after the final round of feedback. By writer the extent of the increase ranges from 3 percentage points for Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to 46 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5, and by grader it ranges from 13 percentage points for Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash to 32 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5. When a model grades its own writing the score tends to be about 9 percentage points higher than the average of what the other models give it. About half of the difference that we see from round to round is within the grader's own noise. Feedback generally results in the highest marks, but even just having the chance to revise, or having the additional budget, in terms of time or tool calls, without any feedback, results in considerable increases for some of the models but not for others. We find that how much such a loop helps depends on which model plays which role, but weaker models generally do not improve stronger models.

papers.title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
papers.abstract: Virtual trials use routinely collected clinical data to evaluate treatment strategies, but translating a study protocol into an executable analysis requires determining how clinical concepts and study requirements should be represented in the available data and applied consistently across the workflow. These decisions depend on local data representations and operational conventions and can involve source selection, patient and encounter identity, linkage, and temporal interpretation. Here we introduce VirtualTrialHarness (VTHarness), an agent framework that coordinates virtual-trial operationalization by selecting reusable procedural skills for each workflow stage and uses explicit contracts to maintain consistent study decisions across stages. We also introduce VTBenchmark for evaluating source selection and cohort construction. Across three complex synthetic environments, VTHarness successfully produced all required cohort outputs matching the references in 95.1% of workflows after requirement clarification, compared with 60.4% using retrieval from the same procedural corpus. Procedural skills improved source recovery across three language models and increased source overlap with analyst code in 13 Mayo Clinic cases. Site-specific adaptation enabled reference-matched cohort execution across eight MIMIC-IV tasks. Within the Mayo Clinic Virtual Trials Program, the framework supported investigator review of cohort construction and endpoint analysis. These findings support coordinating procedural guidance with workflow decisions to improve virtual-trial implementation across complex clinical schemas.

papers.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Across three benchmarks, AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene on large evaluation sets, and its advantage widens as the set shrinks toward a few hundred items. It remains accurate as pools grow more uneven, a label-free dispersion statistic indicates in advance when trust weighting helps, and its learned trust weights track per-judge human validity.

translation.title: AGORA：基于项目反应理论的可靠性感知 LLM 评审聚合方法
translation.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge 是昂贵人工评估的常见替代方案，而聚合多个评审是缓解单一评审偏差的标准做法。评审池中混合了可靠性差异极大的评审，而用于验证它们的人工标注集通常只有几百条或更少。在这种情形下，逐项平均会给予弱评审与强评审同等的权重，而 Dawid-Skene 等混淆表模型则必须从过少的样本中估计每个评审的错误表。我们提出 AGORA（Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments），一个基于项目反应理论（item-response theory）的聚合器，它将所有条目置于同一潜在质量尺度上，并用一个敏感度参数和有序评分阈值来刻画每个评审，从而无需人工标注即可从所有条目中联合学习评审可靠性。在三个基准上，AGORA 在大规模评估集上与 Dawid-Skene 相当或更优，且当评估集缩小到几百条时其优势进一步扩大。当评审池愈发不均衡时它仍保持准确，一个无需标注的离散度统计量可以预先指示何时启用信任加权有帮助，且其学到的信任权重与各评审的人工验证有效性相吻合。
translation.brief: 针对小规模标注下多 LLM 评审聚合中弱评审权重过高的问题，提出基于项目反应理论的 AGORA，无需人工标注即可联合学习各评审的可靠性与条目质量。

papers.title: What Do We Mean When We Say 'F*ck AI'?: Moral Panic, Semantic Indeterminacy, and the Reification of Techno-Capitalism
papers.abstract: Academic and (increasingly) public resistance to artificial intelligence (AI) often blurs the line between legitimate critique of techno-capitalist exploitation and (inflated) existential risk. Moreover, discourse around AI can sometimes resemble a "moral panic" where an apparently clear and identifiable scapegoat is targeted in lieu of the complex systemic problems that are causing (genuine and justified) social anxieties. However, AI is not a monolith. In this paper, we explore the environmental, political, and socio-technical consequences of the semantic indeterminacy of discourse about "AI" in conjunction with the increasing moral panic encompassing these technologies. We argue that since the umbrella term "AI" lacks a coherent, singular referent, the moral panic about AI inadvertently reifies the concept of an autonomous, singular agent with inherent and often autonomous tendencies, which aligns with corporate narratives. Hence, well-intentioned critique, activist pushback, and public protest paradoxically amplifies hype-based discussions of AI, thus validating the "threat" narrative that tech leaders deploy to exaggerate their products' capabilities and market value, further consolidating and centralising their political and socio-economic power. Moreover, if "AI" does not refer to a unified class of technologies, then policy intended to govern "AI" will systematically (and necessarily) fail. We conclude by proposing ways forward to improve AI literacy, enforce accountability, and repurpose existing regulation in order to imagine a more positive AI future.

translation.title: 当我们说“F*ck AI”时，我们指的是什么？：道德恐慌、语义不确定性与技术资本主义的物化
translation.abstract: 学术界以及日益增多的公众对人工智能（AI）的抵制，常常模糊了对技术资本主义剥削的正当批判与（被夸大的）生存风险之间的界限。此外，围绕 AI 的话语有时类似于一场“道德恐慌”，即把一个看似清晰可辨的替罪羊当作靶子，以替代那些引发（真实且合理的）社会焦虑的复杂系统性问题。然而，AI 并非铁板一块。本文探讨了“AI”话语的语义不确定性所带来的环境、政治与社会技术后果，以及围绕这些技术日益加剧的道德恐慌。我们认为，由于“AI”这一伞形术语缺乏连贯、单一的指涉对象，针对 AI 的道德恐慌无意中物化了“一个具有内在且常常自主倾向的自主单一智能体”这一概念，而这恰恰契合了企业的叙事。因此，善意的批判、活动人士的抵制和公众抗议反而悖论式地放大了基于炒作的 AI 讨论，从而印证了科技领袖用来夸大其产品能力和市场价值的“威胁”叙事，进一步巩固并集中了他们的政治与社会经济权力。此外，如果“AI”并不指涉一类统一的技术，那么旨在治理“AI”的政策将系统性地（且必然地）失败。最后，我们提出了改进 AI 素养、强化问责以及重新利用现有监管的可行路径，以构想一个更积极的 AI 未来。
translation.brief: 针对“AI”一词语义模糊导致道德恐慌反而强化企业炒作叙事的问题，通过批判性话语分析论证统一治理 AI 的政策必然失效，并提出提升 AI 素养与问责的改进路径。

papers.title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games
papers.abstract: We study repeated general games over $T$ rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints couple the players' decisions across rounds. Without budgets, low swap regret simultaneously guarantees the learner sublinear regret and caps the optimizer at its Stackelberg value. Budgets break this picture: adversarial no-regret becomes impossible, so the natural goals are non-manipulability---no adaptive optimizer earns more than $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + o(T)$, where $\mathtt{BSE}$ is its Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium value---and low stochastic regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. We give an efficient, budget-feasible learning algorithm that achieves both goals in every budgeted game: any adaptive optimizer, budgeted or not, earns at most $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + O(\sqrt{T})$ in expectation, and if the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy on each of a constant number of intervals, the learner has $O(\sqrt{T})$ regret on each such interval. Our learner best responds to forecasts of the optimizer's play that are calibrated in two novel senses, since under budgets the calibration that prevents manipulation no longer yields low stochastic regret. Response calibration, which conditions on the learner's own mixed response by embedding its continuous mixing weight as a step function in $L^2([-1,1])$, prevents manipulation without discretizing responses; dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration ensures low regret. Although low calibration error requires randomized forecasts---distributions over a continuous space that need not have a succinct representation or be directly computable---we construct such forecasts in polynomial time by simulating online gradient ascent.

translation.title: 预算约束博弈中的学习型与最优化型玩家
translation.abstract: 我们研究在 $T$ 轮重复的一般博弈中，一个效用最大化的最优化者与一个学习型智能体之间的交互，其中预算约束将双方在各轮的决策耦合在一起。在没有预算时，低 swap regret 同时保证学习者的次线性遗憾，并将最优化者的收益限制在其 Stackelberg 值。预算打破了这一图景：对抗性 no-regret 变得不可能，因此自然的目标是非可操纵性——任何自适应最优化者的收益不超过 $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + o(T)$，其中 $\mathtt{BSE}$ 是其预算化 Stackelberg 均衡（Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium）值——以及当最优化者采用固定混合策略时的低随机遗憾。我们给出一个高效且预算可行的学习算法，在每个预算化博弈中同时实现这两个目标：任何自适应最优化者（无论是否有预算）的期望收益至多为 $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + O(\sqrt{T})$；若最优化者在常数个区间上各采用固定混合策略，则学习者在每个区间上的遗憾为 $O(\sqrt{T})$。我们的学习者对最优化者行为的预测做出最优响应，这些预测在两种新颖意义上是校准的，因为在预算约束下，防止操纵的校准不再能带来低随机遗憾。响应校准（response calibration）通过将学习者自身的连续混合权重作为 $L^2([-1,1])$ 中的阶梯函数嵌入、以其自身混合响应为条件，在不离散化响应的情况下防止操纵；对偶加权拉格朗日校准（dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration）则确保低遗憾。尽管低校准误差需要随机化预测——即连续空间上未必有简洁表示或可直接计算的分布——我们通过模拟在线梯度上升在多项式时间内构造出这样的预测。
translation.brief: 针对预算约束重复博弈中学习型智能体既要防操纵又要低遗憾的问题，提出基于两种新型校准预测的高效预算可行学习算法，同时实现非可操纵性与区间级次线性遗憾。

papers.title: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system
papers.abstract: As autonomous AI agents enter permissionless onchain markets, selecting new service providers remains a core challenge. Existing reputation systems depend on scarce resources like human curation, identity credentials, or voluntary reviews, while naive volume rankings are vulnerable to Sybil attacks. We evaluate whether existing onchain payment histories can yield provider ratings that are resilient against Sybil attacks. Using a 157-day dataset comprising 66M agentic transactions worth $6.1M across 16 blockchains, we model payment flows as a bipartite graph between buyers and providers. A provider's rating is derived from graph paths linked to a buyer's existing trusted network. We propose three Sybil-resistant rating algorithms: a max-flow rating and two relaxed algorithms optimized for stronger rating performance. Evaluating these algorithms against simulated adversaries across 813 buyers, we show that rating manipulation costs 20% of those buyers' total spend and is around 23x harder to manipulate than the standard similarity rule (collaborative filtering).

translation.title: Anduin：一个抗女巫攻击的智能体市场声誉系统
translation.abstract: 随着自主 AI 智能体进入无需许可的链上市场，如何选择新的服务提供者仍是核心挑战。现有声誉系统依赖于稀缺资源，如人工筛选、身份凭证或自愿评价，而简单的交易量排名容易受到女巫（Sybil）攻击。我们评估现有的链上支付历史能否产生抗女巫攻击的服务提供者评分。基于一个涵盖 16 条区块链、6600 万笔总价值 610 万美元智能体交易、历时 157 天的数据集，我们将支付流建模为买方与服务提供者之间的二部图。服务提供者的评分由连接到买方既有可信网络的图路径推导得出。我们提出三种抗女巫攻击的评分算法：一个最大流评分算法和两个为更强评分性能而优化的松弛算法。在 813 个买方上针对模拟对手评估这些算法，结果表明操纵评分的成本为这些买方总消费的 20%，且比标准相似度规则（协同过滤）难操纵约 23 倍。
translation.brief: 针对链上智能体市场中声誉系统易受女巫攻击的问题，将支付历史建模为二部图并提出基于图路径的三种抗女巫评分算法。

papers.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
papers.abstract: What should ``verified'' mean when evaluating LLM-generated code? Many existing pipelines report a single verification number. We argue this collapses three distinct properties measured in a conditional audit sequence: verifier acceptance (Surface A), \emph{syntactic specification binding (Surface B: does the proof obligation bind to the spec?), and \emph{semantic specification fidelity} (Surface C: does the spec capture the informal requirement?). Two empirical demonstrations show the surfaces separate. \textbf{First ($A \neq B$), via Li@Opus (a same-model reproduction of \citet{li2025dafny}'s Dafny-as-intermediate-representation (IR) pipeline under Claude Opus 4.7) on three Python benchmarks}: it reaches \textbf{99.1\% verifier acceptance} on HumanEval while only \textbf{1.9\%} carry a certificate binding to a spec-defined predicate or function. \textbf{Second ($B \neq C$), via VCG on two Rust benchmarks}: we use VCG (which is our own in-house Dafny-as-intermediate pipeline) on Rust because the Rust target lets us enforce fully-verifiable output (every component ships as a Dafny certificate, ensures-binding gate passing by construction). Even inside that construction, \textbf{11.48\% (MBPP-Rust) and 14.82\% (VeriContest LC slice) of structurally-verified samples still fail hidden tests}. On the LC slice of VeriContest, \textbf{VCG's reported End2End rate is 7.79\% (535/6870).} The cited external rates are 5.51\% (GPT-5.5) and 1.88\% (single-shot Opus 4.7). These give descriptive differences of 2.3 percentage points and 4.14$\times$, respectively; task-budget, repair and harness differences prevent a matched-performance claim.

translation.title: 已验证却空洞：LLM 驱动的验证式代码生成的三种失效面
translation.abstract: 在评估 LLM 生成的代码时，“已验证”究竟应意味着什么？许多现有流水线只报告一个单一的验证数字。我们认为这混淆了在条件化审计序列中测量的三种不同属性：验证器接受（Surface A）、句法层面的规范绑定（Surface B：证明义务是否绑定到规范？）以及语义层面的规范保真度（Surface C：规范是否捕捉了非形式化需求？）。两个实证演示表明这些层面是相互分离的。第一（$A \neq B$），通过 Li@Opus（在 Claude Opus 4.7 下对 \citet{li2025dafny} 的 Dafny 作为中间表示（IR）流水线的同模型复现）在三个 Python 基准上进行：它在 HumanEval 上达到 99.1% 的验证器接受率，但仅有 1.9% 携带绑定到规范定义谓词或函数的证书。第二（$B \neq C$），通过 VCG 在两个 Rust 基准上进行：我们在 Rust 上使用 VCG（我们自研的 Dafny 作为中间表示的流水线），因为 Rust 目标使我们能够强制完全可验证的输出（每个组件都以 Dafny 证书交付，ensures 绑定门控在构造上即通过）。即便在这种构造下，仍有 11.48%（MBPP-Rust）和 14.82%（VeriContest LC 切片）的结构上已验证样本在隐藏测试中失败。在 VeriContest 的 LC 切片上，VCG 报告的 End2End 率为 7.79%（535/6870）。所引用的外部结果为 5.51%（GPT-5.5）和 1.88%（单次 Opus 4.7）。这分别给出 2.3 个百分点和 4.14 倍的描述性差异；任务预算、修复和测试框架的差异使得无法做出匹配性能的断言。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 验证式代码生成中“验证器通过”被当作单一指标的问题，提出将验证分解为验证器接受、规范绑定与规范保真度三个失效面，并用 Python 与 Rust 实验证明三者相互分离。

papers.title: RIDGE: State-Conditioned Reward Blending for Behavioral Coverage in Deep RL Game Agents
papers.abstract: A deep RL agent trained on a fixed persona reward plays one way: an Explorer keeps exploring while starving, a Survivor hoards on an empty map. Since each persona fixes its own reward, automated playtesting trains N agents for N styles. Changing reward composition mid-episode runs into the switching-stability dilemma: PPO degrades under non-stationary rewards. We present RIDGE, a single-agent architecture that sidesteps the dilemma with two design choices: a state-conditioned blender that computes softmax-normalized sigmoid weights from slow-moving state variables, and a multi-head critic that trains one value head per persona on its own stationary signal. On Crafter with four personas, one \ridge agent acquires both branches of the wood-tier crafting/combat split that no fixed-persona baseline solves jointly, and a sharpness ablation confirms state-conditioning drives the gain. We position these results as demonstrations of the blending mechanism's dynamics across n=3 seeds per condition; larger multi-seed sweeps remain future work.

papers.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) to consolidate capabilities from multiple teachers. Although prior work reports near-perfect in-distribution (IND) distillation performance, we find that this can mask incomplete capability consolidation beyond the supervised distribution. A preliminary study on synthetic reasoning shows that OPD does not fully transfer teachers' generalization capabilities. We then extend this investigation to real-world tasks, evaluating extrapolative and compositional generalization across mathematical reasoning, coding, agent, and long-context capabilities using Qwen3 models. Across extrapolative settings, OPD and MOPD reach 96.04-102.73% of their teachers' IND scores. Yet their out-of-distribution (OOD) scores remain 2.45-16.25% below the base model's. Across three compositional settings, MOPD improves IND performance over the base model, but its performance on composed tasks as OOD remains 18.19-24.34% below that of the best teachers. To understand these gaps, we examine teacher capability and data coverage as two potential bottlenecks. Jointly alleviating these bottlenecks eliminates OOD forgetting in our experiments and suggests the potential for generalization beyond the teacher. (M)OPD also reduces OOD forgetting on average relative to its reinforcement learning (RL) baselines. Analysis of the associated update geometry reveals smaller and more spectrally concentrated updates on average than those of the RL baselines, along with greater shared update structure under MOPD. Motivated by these findings, we propose geometry-based patching and base-preserving replay to improve OOD performance while largely preserving IND performance. Our findings identify a blind spot in capability consolidation via (M)OPD, highlighting the need for algorithms that explicitly support OOD retention and generalization.

papers.title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. Model-free drafters provide no per-token confidence, so they cannot take part in budget allocation, and deployments must either fix one drafter or split their GPUs between drafters. We present \sys, a framework that runs a model-based and a model-free drafter on every step and gives each request the better of their chains, within adaptive verification and entirely on the GPU, which keeps asynchronous scheduling intact. The key idea is a price per verified draft token: the goodput that slot would earn elsewhere in the batch. Once the model-free drafter's tokens carry calibrated acceptance estimates, fit once on general text, this price puts both drafters' chains on one scale. translation.title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter
translation.abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. Model-free drafters provide no per-token confidence, so they cannot take part in budget allocation, and deployments must either fix one drafter or split their GPUs between drafters. We present \sys, a framework that runs a model-based and a model-free drafter on every step and gives each request the better of their chains, within adaptive verification and entirely on the GPU, which keeps asynchronous scheduling intact. The key idea is a price per verified draft token: the goodput that slot would earn elsewhere in the batch. Once the model-free drafter's tokens carry calibrated acceptance estimates, fit once on general text, this price puts both drafters' chains on one scale. Instantiated with \dspark and an n-gram drafter in vLLM, \sys achieves 1.10--1.62\x the output throughput of \dspark on code editing at batch size~4 and 1.04--1.27\x at batch size~128, while staying at 0.97--1.01\x of it on chat at temperature~0. A single deployment can therefore serve both workloads.

papers.title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
papers.abstract: On Replit, our agentic engineering platform, users now build entire products without writing code, through successive feature requests to an agent. Yet existing coding benchmarks evaluate single, fully specified tasks, and many are near saturation. We introduce ViBench 2.0, a benchmark for long-horizon software building that we use to select our platform's models. Its 17 full-stack web products, modeled on widely used software, grow over 241 feature requests and are judged only when finished, as a user would judge them: a browser agent runs 544 test plans, and a build passes only if every plan does, under a grading protocol validated to keep this strict score reliable. Evaluating nine models, we find a reliability gap: the three strongest pass up to 98% of test plans yet deliver a fully working product in at most 65% of builds, and no open-weight model delivers one. The gap is closing fast: across three releases of one model family, pass@1 on the public products rises from 3% to 53% while the cost per build falls by more than half. We release eight products with the harness and grader, hold out nine, and report lessons from production use.

papers.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
papers.abstract: Autonomous software agents can act through tools, delegate work, and change their models or execution environments while earlier authorizations remain in flight. We present Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA), an approach designed to be harness-independent, for maintaining operational authority according to currently justified assurance. It distinguishes evidence validity from contextual applicability, derives assurance claims from eligible evidence, and resolves a multidimensional effective-authority envelope within a principal-declared ceiling and applicable policy. A typed dependency graph supports selective re-evaluation of authorization-relevant changes. An authority epoch changes when effective authority changes; a distinct optional authorization-basis version supports revalidation of action-specific authorization conditions. Protected effect-time enforcement can reject stale actions before a consequential resource change, subject to the available commit mechanism. A compositional Domain Governance Profile expresses domain-specific semantics without granting authority. Controlled scenario tests implemented as a regression suite using a trading profile exercise default-deny rules, evidence-conditioned contraction and recovery, policy divergence, selective non-response, and stale-action rejection at a local gateway before the simulated-broker boundary. The study establishes implementation-level evidence in one domain, not a cross-domain guarantee of harmful-behavior prevention.

papers.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: The memory of production agents is increasingly becoming a bottleneck and is built almost exclusively from text: key points are extracted from out-of-limit context and retrieved into context at query time. Therefore, every new query incurs an additional cost that grows with the accumulated history. Weight memory is a complementary alternative that internalizes knowledge into model parameters and answers with no context at all, and has recently proven effective in self-evolving agents for internalizing skills and behaviors. However, its application in episodic and semantic memory, such as user-specific facts, remains comparatively unexplored, and a gap remains between earlier attempts at weight memory and text-based systems regarding recall performance. We study how to make weight memory competitive as a long-term factual store by applying on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). It trains a context-free student from a teacher, which is the same model conditioned on the user's memory, together with a verify-then-regenerate router that lets weight and text memory each cover the queries they handle best. On the HaluMem benchmark, OPSD matches or surpasses strong text-memory baselines, including full-context prompting and retrieval systems, while reading fewer tokens per query. We further conduct an extensive study that characterizes the behavior of weight memory and analyzes how different training recipes affect its performance. As agent harnesses move toward persistent, multi-session deployments, these results position weight memory as a practical, low-cost component of agent memory and provide insights into feasible training and evaluation protocols for combining it with retrieval.

papers.title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
papers.abstract: Conversational video characters must generate video as fast as it plays, for one user at a time: at 24 fps, a sustained 166.7 ms per four-frame chunk at batch size one, with only a few chunks of buffering. We describe the system behind Runway Characters, which serves a $\approx$57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer (four denoising passes per chunk) at 704$\times$1088 and 24 fps on four H100 GPUs with a voice agent in the loop. Each chunk takes 240 attention calls, each reading a 5,788-slot KV cache in which only 757 tokens are new, and 29% of the original step was whole-cache work repeated in every call. We move that work to write time (a ring cache, RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, and a delta rotation when positions reset), fuse the tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM with in-switch reduction, and give the decoder that turns latents into video frames its own GPU. Without the fused kernel, our optimizations cut the diffusion step from 240.9 to 159.3 ms (1.51$\times$, 24.5 fps sustained) with no detected degradation in lip-sync scores; the fused kernel, rolled back once in production and since re-enabled, reaches 147.4 ms (1.63$\times$, 43% of FP8 peak). In seven weeks of production the worker averaged above 23.5 fps in 99.5% of sessions that streamed for at least a second, and our pipeline takes 0.49 s of a 2.1 s median conversational turn. On the same GPUs, the two open-source real-time video systems we benchmarked, at four denoising passes, miss real time or add over a second of latency (one by estimate), at a third to half of our resolution.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Scaling-Law Discovery for Recommendation Systems via Coupled Hyperparameter Scaling
papers.abstract: Large-scale ranking and recommendation models of Web platforms benefit from increased compute much as large language models do, and their scaling behavior is broadly power-law in form. Yet ranking models have heterogeneous architectures which makes their scaling law less straightforward than that of LLMs. We address how to discover the scaling law of an arbitrary ranking model efficiently. We introduce a scaling layer, which groups primitive architecture parameters into semantically coherent groups and defines how they co-vary, inducing a mapping from a low-dimensional space of hyper-hyperparameters into the full architecture space. On top of it, Axia fits scaling-informed surrogates, selects configurations by a posterior-based acquisition criterion, and returns a Pareto frontier from which per-model operating points are validated -- replacing exhaustive sweeps with a small number of informative runs. A fleet-level evaluation protocol, computed on a fixed representative model set under matched trial budgets, makes refinements to either component measurable. Our contribution is an automated system that learns model-specific complexity-quality relationships and gives uncertainty-aware guidance for allocating compute across a heterogeneous model ecosystem. Across 34 model iterations in two development cycles on Meta's ads ranking and retrieval system, the workflow yielded a mean 0.66% offline normalized-entropy improvement and 0.36% cumulative online lift.

papers.title: Attributing Agent Failures to Their History Needs an Executed Counterfactual: Toward a Reporting Standard
papers.abstract: Published explanations of why long-horizon agents fail are commonly taxonomies labeled over completed trajectories: a judge reads a transcript and names the failure. We argue that a claim attributing an agent's behavior to its history should carry intervention-verified evidence, per instance or via a validated estimator: freeze an executable mid-trajectory state, alter only the history the agent sees, and continue - executed rather than inferred from the transcript, at a state whose restoration has been measured, with a replay certificate matched to the estimand. Each of the four manipulation classes we name has a precedent, and several methods already execute interventions from checkpoints, re-executed prefixes or recorded conversation states (for example DoVer, REFLECT, Min et al., Who&When Pro, Causal Agent Replay), but none reports a measured replay certificate. Two cautionary measurements, neither applying the standard, follow: a carrier taxonomy whose "concentration" could not be separated from benchmark construction (adjusted odds ratio 1.15, interval crossing 1), and hash-identical snapshots that, restored into identically seeded processes, agreed with one another in 24 of 24 states while differing from the live continuation in 9 and 20 of 24. Restoring the captured position of a random stream made all 24 agree with the live run.

papers.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
papers.abstract: Evaluating open-ended agent tasks increasingly falls to an Agent-as-a-Judge: an evaluator handed tools and the agent's full trajectory so it can verify a result against the environment. The premise is that a judge that gathers its own evidence should be grounded by it. We show that this grounding does not immunize the judge against confirmation bias: a single false pre-screening note, attributed to an authority and carrying no evidential bearing on the correct verdict, overturns up to 40% of a tool-using judge's correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets, even though the judge collects decisive evidence. The shift is driven by specific properties of the cue. We treat this cue as a controlled diagnostic of confirmation bias rather than an adversarial attack. Our central contribution is to explain how confirmation bias changes the judge's behavior in a trajectory. We classify changes in judge behavior and attribute changes to one of three failure modes: over-trust (verify, conclude correctly, then defer), hallucination (fabricate support for the flip), and under-investigation (stop at the first corroborating signal). For the two Claude judges, the failure is predominantly over-trust (67-75% of harmful flips), while smaller judges have error modes spread across all three. Lightweight mitigations blunt but never remove the bias.
